Who we are

A care team that comes to you, because there is no place like home to heal.

Royal Home Health Care, Inc. is a licensed, Medicare-certified home health agency right here in Van Nuys. We believe getting great medical care should not mean sitting in traffic or staying in a hospital room longer than you have to. Our nurses, therapists, and aides bring attentive care and medical supplies straight to your front door.

Every care plan is shaped around your real life, including your health needs, your daily routine, your family, and your doctor's recommendations. We stay in close touch with your physician so everyone is working together toward your recovery.

  • Your doctor leads

    Every visit follows the care plan signed by your physician.

  • We come to you

    Nurses, therapists, and aides visit you in your own home.

  • One connected team

    Nursing, therapy, and supplies coordinated under one roof.

What we offer

Hospital-level skill, delivered with a neighbor's warmth.

From IV therapy to stroke recovery, every service is ordered by your physician and coordinated by one team.

Skilled Nursing Services

Hands-on clinical care from our registered nurses, brought right to your living room under your doctor's orders.

  • Wound Care

    Gentle assessment, cleaning, and dressing for surgical incisions, pressure injuries, and diabetic ulcers, plus practical guidance for care between visits.

    Learn more

  • IV Therapy

    Doctor-ordered IV antibiotics, hydration fluids, and infusions given safely in your living room, complete with PICC line and port care.

    Learn more

  • PleurX™ Catheter Drainage

    Scheduled, sterile drainage for indwelling pleural or abdominal catheters at home so you can breathe easier and avoid hospital trips.

    Learn more

  • Catheter Care

    Private, respectful urinary catheter changes, irrigation, and troubleshooting at home, including Foley and suprapubic catheters.

    Learn more

  • Vitamin B12 Injections

    Doctor-ordered vitamin B12 injections given comfortably at home for pernicious anemia and B12 deficiency, with ongoing symptom checks.

    Learn more

  • Insulin & Diabetic (DM) Injections

    Calm, hands-on support with insulin and injectable diabetes medications at home, including blood sugar checks and one-on-one coaching.

    Learn more

Recovery & Condition Programs

Focused nursing, therapy, and family support tailored around a specific diagnosis, surgery, or hospital stay.

  • Hospital Discharge Care

    A calm, organized transition from hospital to home, starting with a medication review, vital sign check, and clear answers on day one.

    Learn more

  • Post-Surgical Recovery

    Skilled nursing and rehabilitation after joint replacement, heart, abdominal, or spine surgery, covering incision care, pain control, and safe mobility.

    Learn more

  • Stroke Recovery

    Coordinated nursing, physical, occupational, and speech therapy at home to rebuild strength, speech, and daily confidence after a stroke.

    Learn more

  • Diabetes Management

    One-on-one diabetes coaching, blood sugar tracking, foot and skin checks, and medication support so you feel steady and in control at home.

    Learn more

  • Homebound & Bedbound Care

    Attentive skilled nursing, skin protection, gentle repositioning, and caregiver support for patients who stay mostly in bed or at home.

    Learn more

  • Cardiac Care

    Heart failure and post-heart-surgery nursing at home, including blood pressure checks, daily weight tracking, and medication support.

    Learn more

  • Fall Risk & Mobility

    Home safety walkthroughs, medication reviews, and in-home balance and strength therapy so you can move around your house with confidence.

    Learn more

  • Not sure which program fits?

    Tell us about the diagnosis or hospital stay. A registered nurse will help you sort out next steps.

Medicare-Certified Home Health Agency

$0 out of pocket for covered home health visits with Medicare.

Because we are a Medicare-certified agency, Original Medicare pays 100% of the cost for covered home health visits when you qualify. You typically qualify if:

  • You need part-time or intermittent skilled nursing or rehabilitation therapy
  • You are considered homebound, meaning leaving home takes a major effort or requires assistance
  • Your doctor or allowed provider has seen you recently and ordered home health care
  • Your care is provided by a Medicare-certified agency like Royal Home Health Care

For durable medical equipment like walkers or hospital beds, Medicare typically covers 80% and you pay 20% after the Part B deductible. We also work with Medi-Cal, select private insurance plans, workers' compensation, regional centers, and private pay.

How it works

Getting started is easier than you think.

  1. 01

    Step 1: Quick referral

    Your doctor, hospital, or clinic sends a referral over, or you call us directly and we reach out to your doctor's office for you.

  2. 02

    Step 2: Home nurse visit

    One of our registered nurses comes to your home, listens to how you are feeling, and goes over your medications and care needs.

  3. 03

    Step 3: Your personal care plan

    Together with your physician, we set up a plan that fits your life, including the right services, visit schedule, and recovery goals.

  4. 04

    Step 4: Care that adjusts with you

    Your team visits on schedule, shows your family how to help, keeps your doctor updated, and adjusts your visits as you get stronger.

Who can refer?

You or a family member · A friend or neighbor · Your doctor or nurse practitioner · A hospital, skilled nursing facility, clinic, or social service agency

Why home health care

Recovery feels different in your own living room.

Most people heal better when they can sleep in their own bed, eat their own food, and recover surrounded by family on a schedule that fits real life.

  • Familiar surroundings

    You get to heal in your own bed and living room, surrounded by the people and daily routines you love.

  • Guided by your doctor

    Your own physician stays in charge. Every visit follows a care plan built with and signed by your doctor.

  • A smoother transition home

    Coming home from the hospital feels much less stressful when a nurse is right there to review your medications and answer questions.

  • Fewer trips back to the hospital

    Steady check-ins at home help catch small changes early and keep overall healthcare costs down.

Questions, answered

What families ask us most.

See all FAQs

How do I know if I qualify?

Anyone under a doctor's care who needs skilled medical support at home may qualify. For Medicare to cover it, you need part-time or intermittent skilled care, you must be considered homebound, and your doctor or allowed provider needs to see you and sign off on a home health care plan. Give us a call and one of our registered nurses will gladly talk through your situation and check your eligibility.

See Medicare eligibility

What will I pay with Medicare?

If you qualify under Original Medicare, you pay $0 out of pocket for covered home health visits. If your doctor orders durable medical equipment like a walker, wheelchair, or hospital bed, Medicare typically covers 80% and you pay 20% of the Medicare-approved amount after meeting your Part B deductible.

What does “homebound” mean?

Being homebound does not mean you are stuck in bed all day. It simply means leaving home is not recommended because of your health condition, or you need support like a walker, wheelchair, special transportation, or another person's help to go out, and leaving takes a real physical effort. You can still leave home for doctor visits, religious services, adult day care, and occasional family outings.

Do you provide 24-hour or live-in care?

No. Home health care is built around scheduled, part-time clinical visits. However, you are never on your own after hours. A registered nurse is always on call by phone in the evenings, on weekends, and on holidays.

Who can refer me to Royal Home Health Care?

You can call us directly yourself, or a family member or friend can reach out on your behalf. Your doctor, hospital discharge planner, skilled nursing facility, clinic, or social worker can also send a referral. Once you call, we reach out to your doctor's office to take care of the paperwork and orders.
